text:
Samir Patel: @channel AcmeAI reporting a sudden throughput regression on their dedicated pool starting ~01:10 UTC. Token/sec dropped ~60%, 95th latency climbed from ~0.9s -> 2.3s. They're also intermittently seeing 429s and a few 500s. Ticket INC-4921. Attaching quick metrics and a minimal log excerpt below.

DevOps Bot: [autoscale] pool:acme-dedicated-42 scale_down_requested at 2026-03-17T01:12:04Z; scale_up none. CPU/GPU utilization flapping: GPU avg 32% -> 48% after 01:05 UTC.

Kevin Liu: Thanks Samir. Did the customer's traffic shape change? any long-context jobs spiking?

Samir Patel: No, they said same workload. 90% of requests are short convo turns (<=128 tokens). Spike in prefill latency and prefill queue depth. p50 tokens/time flat. p95 prefill queue wait up.

Tayla Morgan: @Kevin @Alex I looked at the runtime timeline. We started seeing many tiny microbatches piling up on a node; continuous-batcher seems to be emitting very small windows. Possible cause: max_batch_tokens config lowered on that pool? Or packer mis-sorting by token size.

Alex Gomez: Hypothesis: particle scheduling + max_batch_tokens cap created many underfilled batches. If continuous-batcher prefers fill-by-token and max_batch_tokens was set low (e.g., 256) while typical small requests are 64 tokens, we end up with many tiny microbatches and more scheduling overhead. Also KV cache churn can fragment coalescing.

Samir Patel: I pulled the pool config:
```
pool: acme-dedicated-42
continuous_batcher:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_tokens: 256
  batch_window_ms: 6
  pack_strategy: sort_by_size
```
Looks standard but the pack strategy was recently changed to sort_by_size in canary two days ago.

Kevin Liu: That matches. If sort_by_size sends many small short requests early, packer might create many tiny batches because it tries to keep token-sum balanced across windows. Can we see batch size histogram?

Samir Patel: Batch size histogram (1h around regression): majority are 1-2 request batches; avg batch tokens ~130, avg queue wait 420ms. Before change avg batch tokens ~480, avg queue wait 90ms.

DevOps Bot: [metric] alarm: acme-dedicated-42.prefill_queue_wait.p95 breached threshold (300ms) at 2026-03-17T01:09:58Z.

Alex Gomez: Repro plan: force pack_strategy: fifo on a canary node in pool and run live traffic split 10%. If throughput improves and p95 latency drops, revert pack strategy in rollout. Also try bumping max_batch_tokens->1024 temporarily to see effect.

Tayla Morgan: Agreed. Also check autoscaler thresholds: node utilization may be below scale_up because per-node GPU load low (due to tiny batches) even though overall pool throughput low. We might need to add a policy to scale on prefill_queue_wait in addition to GPU util.

Support Escalations: I attached the customer's request traces and a short screen recording: https://files.redwood/acme/inc-4921/trace.mp4. They captured the 429s sequence. Customer is demanding ETA for mitigation.

Kevin Liu: Action items: (1) Alex canary packer change -> pack_strategy: fifo on 1/8 nodes (Samir please coordinate), (2) Tayla open autoscale tweak RFC: consider queue-wait based scale triggers, (3) Support escalate customer with temporary mitigation note (bump max_batch_tokens) and ask them to accept short canary.

Samir Patel: Canary started at 01:38 UTC with pack_strategy:fifo on node n-gpu-07. Early signs: avg batch tokens up to ~400, prefill p95 -> 180ms. No customer-visible errors yet. Will monitor for 30m then roll if stable.

Alex Gomez: If canary is green, plan to roll config and revert the last sort_by_size canary. Also follow-up to investigate why KV cache eviction rate spiked around same time (could worsen packing).

Tayla Morgan: Filed ENG-OPS-786: autoscale should consider prefill_queue_wait and microburst detection.

Support Escalations: Update to customer sent: "We're running a targeted canary to improve packing and reduce queue wait. Expect improvements in <45min. We'll keep you posted." :thumbsup:

Samir Patel: Update at 02:05 UTC: canary roll to 25% nodes. p95 prefill queue wait down to 120ms, throughput recovered ~55% vs regression baseline. Customer reports far fewer 429s. Closing immediate escalation, follow-ups: autoscale RFC, revert sort_by_size canary, dig into KV eviction correlate.

Kevin Liu: Nice work. Please file a postmortem with timeline and config diffs once everything stable.

Alex Gomez: I'll capture the batch histograms and attach diffs to the postmortem.

Samir Patel: Thanks team.
